claims.text: The Bank of Korea's Monetary Policy Decision & Opening Remarks to the Press Conference (16 July 2026) states: "Stock prices underwent a sizable correction amid heightened volatility due to growing concerns over AI investment and large-scale net sales of domestic stocks by foreign investors," and that "financial stability risks also persist," including elevated exchange-rate volatility.

Neither the Bank of Korea nor the Ministry of Economy and Finance has issued a new crisis-level statement since the 29 July 2026 Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting; MOFE's English press-release list shows no stock-market-stabilization item between 30 July and 12 August 2026, and BOK's most recent monetary policy decision remains 16 July 2026 (rate raised 2.50% to 2.75%), with no newer policy statement found as of this check.

South Korea's Ministry of Economy and Finance's press release "Authorities Step Up Swift Coordination and Response Amid Heightened Stock Market Volatility" (29 July 2026) states the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance and Economy convened an Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting attended by the Bank of Korea Governor and the Chairmen of the Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service, after "the recent sharp decline in the stock market, led by semiconductor shares, was driven by intensifying competition in the memory chip industry stemming from China and growing concerns over funding needs among major U.S. technology companies"; the authorities announced investor-specific investment limits on single-stock leveraged products, higher transaction costs, mandatory simulated trading, and a commitment to establish a legal basis for emergency market-stabilization measures.

description: South Korea's KOSPI index, which had surged to an all-time high in June 2026, underwent a sharp correction through July, led by semiconductor shares amid intensifying Chinese competition in the memory-chip industry and concerns over major US technology firms' AI-related funding needs; the slide triggered market-wide trading halts on consecutive sessions in late July. The Bank of Korea's 16 July 2026 policy statement acknowledged a sizable stock-price correction amid heightened volatility and large-scale net sales of domestic stocks by foreign investors. On 29 July the Ministry of Economy and Finance convened an Emergency Market Situation Review Meeting with the Bank of Korea Governor and financial regulators, announcing investment limits on single-stock leveraged products, higher transaction costs, mandatory simulated trading and a commitment to establish a legal basis for emergency market-stabilization measures. With no new crisis-level action from either institution since 29 July, the acute intervention phase has concluded and the episode is assessed as contained.

impact.summary: The KOSPI's semiconductor-led correction prompted an emergency government response on 29 July 2026: the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the Bank of Korea Governor and the heads of the Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service announced curbs on single-stock leveraged products (investment limits, higher transaction costs, mandatory simulated trading) and work on a legal basis for emergency market-stabilization measures, while judging Korea's underlying economic fundamentals solid. Neither institution has issued a new crisis-level statement since 29 July — the Bank of Korea's most recent monetary policy decision remains the 16 July rate rise from 2.50% to 2.75% — and the episode is assessed as contained.

event.scale: National stock market correction; repeated market-wide circuit breakers; emergency government intervention

name: Stock Market Crisis — South Korea

updates.text: With no new crisis-level statement or market action from the Bank of Korea or the Ministry of Economy and Finance since the 29 July emergency measures, the acute intervention phase was judged concluded and the event status moved from ongoing to contained.
